description:
FILED s470bp (Opus, 2026-09-05) from the probe file written for L5 (#1203).
PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by it: the constant-subscript path and the general
path answer the SAME (wrong) thing, which is how it was classified.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bp/probe-slice.pl in the s470bp worktree):

    my @a = (0) x 5;
    my $x = (@a[1..3] = (7,8,9));
    print $x;                      # perl 3 ; PCL ARRAY(0x1)

    my @a = (0) x 5; my @i = (1,2,3);
    my $x = (@a[@i] = (7,8,9));
    print $x;                      # perl 3 ; PCL ARRAY(0x1)  (the twin)

WHY.  A LIST ASSIGNMENT in scalar context yields the number of elements on the
RIGHT-hand side (perlop: "the number of elements produced by the expression on
the right hand side of the assignment").  Both slice-assignment arms of
`p-setf` return `,src-vec` — the source VECTOR — which is right for list
context (perl yields the assigned lvalues there) and stringifies as
`ARRAY(0x…)` in scalar context.

  perl -e 'my @a=(0)x5; my $x = (@a[1..3]=(7,8,9)); print $x'        # 3
  perl -e 'my @a=(0)x5; my @r = (@a[1..3]=(7,8,9)); print scalar @r' # 3

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX is the one `p-hash-=` already has (read it first — rule
11): it returns the flattened contents when `*wantarray*` is T and the input
element COUNT otherwise.  The slice arms need the same two-armed return, with
the count taken from the SOURCE vector's length (not the subscript count:
perl counts the RHS, so `@a[1,2] = (7,8,9)` is 3, not 2 — probed).

Note the LIST-context half also differs from perl in kind: perl yields the
assigned LVALUES (`$_++ for (@a[0,1] = (1,2))` writes through), and PCL yields
the source vector.  Whoever takes this should probe that half too rather than
fix only the scalar one.

SIZE: small, one shape shared by two arms.  It is a CORRECTNESS row, not a
speed one, and it is SILENT — `ARRAY(0x1)` in a numeric comparison is 1.
subject: A slice assignment in SCALAR context yields the source vector, not the COUNT (`my $x = (@a[1..3]=(7,8,9))` prints ARRAY(0x1), perl 3) — PRE-EXISTING, both paths agree; p-hash-= has the two-armed shape to copy
